profiles.name: Randall Duncan Stezer
profiles.description: Randall Duncan Stezer, then 17 and living in Graham, North Carolina, was arrested after the May 1, 2010 anti-capitalist May Day demonstration in downtown Asheville. Stezer was among eleven defendants charged in connection with property damage during the demonstration. He was released on bond on May 5, 2010. Prosecutors later dismissed the charges without leave.
profiles.finding: Denver ABC Asheville defendant list corroborates name; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Dustin Stevens
profiles.description: Dustin Stevens entered the U.S. Army in 2002 and refused to complete 82nd Airborne Division training after concluding that he could not kill. The Army sent him home to await discharge, but a routine traffic stop on January 15, 2009 revealed a military warrant. He was returned to Fort Bragg and held on restriction in the 82nd Holdover Unit while facing a desertion court-martial. Following a public campaign against the unit's conditions and prolonged pretrial restrictions, the Army canceled the court-martial and discharged him in early November 2009.
profiles.finding: Adopt Resistance Dustin Che Stevens account and Omni newsletter corroborate resister. Holloman pharmacy officer photo not linked and rejected.

profiles.name: Juan Galloza Acevedo
profiles.description: Juan Galloza Acevedo was a former member of Los Macheteros who took part in the December 3, 1979 Sabana Seca ambush of a U.S. Navy bus in Puerto Rico. Two sailors, John Ball and Emil White, were killed and ten others were wounded. Investigators identified Galloza Acevedo through evidence developed after the cold case was reopened. He admitted his involvement to federal investigators in July 2013, cooperated, and pleaded guilty to racketeering conspiracy and related murder and robbery conduct. On May 8, 2014, U.S. District Judge Sterling Johnson sentenced him to five years in federal prison, citing his minor role, cooperation, and remorse.
profiles.finding: NotiCel, Primera Hora and CBS corroborate Sabana Seca case; no verified individual portrait located.

profiles.name: Juanito Cordoba-Bermudez
profiles.description: Juanito Cordoba-Bermudez, FARC 57th Front member, was extradited and pleaded guilty to material-support conspiracy. 180 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DEA sentencing release corroborates FARC case; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Katherine Christianson
profiles.description: Katherine Christianson, age 27, pleaded guilty to conspiracy and aiding and abetting in the 2009 ELF-claimed sabotage of US Forest Service tree-genetics research property near Rhinelander, Wisconsin. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Fifth Estate and court opinion corroborate ELF case; genealogy namesake rejected. Existing biography dates merit separate review.

profiles.name: Kyle Shaw
profiles.description: Kyle Shaw, age 19, bombed a Starbucks on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in 2009 and was planning a second bombing when arrested. No one was injured. Sentenced to 42 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: CBS identified case but image URL is starbucks-bombing.jpg, not a verified portrait; image retrieval failed. No photo added.

profiles.name: Pete Perry
profiles.description:
Pete Perry was an anti-war activist who interrupted a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing on Afghanistan and Pakistan on May 21, 2009. He was one of four protesters removed from the hearing and charged. Following an October conviction, he was sentenced December 14 to 45 days with 41 suspended. Nuclear Resister reported that he served the remaining four days over a weekend.

Sources: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/resister/nr154.pdf#page=2 ; https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/resister/nr156.pdf#page=1
profiles.finding: Antiwar biography and Southern Maryland report corroborate activist; historical volunteer and musician namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Laguerre Payen
profiles.description: Laguerre Payen is a Haitian-born Newburgh, New York resident with schizophrenia and an intellectual disability who was recruited by FBI informant Shahed Hussain into the 2009 Newburgh sting. Federal agents arrested Payen and three co-defendants on May 20, 2009. A jury convicted him in October 2010, and Judge Colleen McMahon sentenced him on September 7, 2011 to the mandatory minimum of 25 years in prison followed by five years of supervised release. In July 2023, McMahon reduced the sentence to time served plus 90 days, citing the government-created nature of the plot and Payen's vulnerability. Payen was not released. He was transferred to the federal medical center in Springfield, Missouri, and on January 9, 2024 a federal court ordered his continued civil commitment under 18 U.S.C. § 4246. The Eighth Circuit affirmed that order on July 18, 2025.
profiles.finding: CBS sentencing report corroborates Newburgh case; no individual image in retrieved report. Other image lead lacks reliable origin/credit.

profiles.name: Jorge Abel Ibarguen-Palacio
profiles.description: Jorge Abel Ibarguen-Palacio (Turbo), age 40, was captured in a boat off the coast of Panama in 2009 following a firefight with Panamanian police while attempting to provide weapons to FARC. 130 months federal prison + 2 years specialized release.
profiles.finding: DEA/DOJ and El Heraldo/La Prensa case coverage corroborate identity; no verified individual portrait located.

profiles.name: Yarlei Banol-Ramos
profiles.description: Yarlei Banol-Ramos (Diana), age 35, was captured with Ibarguen-Palacio off Panama in 2009 during a firefight with Panamanian police while attempting to provide weapons to FARC. 180 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DEA sentencing release corroborates identity; no verified individual portrait located.

profiles.name: Hugh F. Farrell
profiles.description: Hugh F. Farrell, age 23, was indicted in 2009 with four misdemeanor counts (intimidation and conversion) plus one Class C felony for involvement in protests against the I-69 highway expansion in Indiana. The judge dismissed the felony racketeering charge in March 2010; his plea bargain was unsupervised probation for two years.
profiles.finding: Denver ABC I-69 legal update corroborates activist. Opera producer headshot not linked and rejected.

profiles.name: Elijah Smith
profiles.description: Elijah Smith was a U.S. servicemember who refused deployment during the Iraq/Afghanistan wars. Iraq War military refuser; pled guilty to desertion. Sentenced to short.
profiles.finding: Sparse profile does not establish reliable identity. Military photographs and UK Smash EDO prisoner not matched to claimed US desertion case; no image added.

profiles.name: Hassan Abu-Jihaad
profiles.description:
Hassan Abu-Jihaad was a Navy signalman who disclosed the location of USS Benfold in an online forum. Authorities taped a phone conversation between Abu-Jihaad and an informant, in which Abu-Jihaad spoke in code regarding the movement of naval ships. Abu-Jihaad was a former roommate of Derrick Shareef, who conspired to attack an Illinois shopping mall and was caught in an FBI sting.

Case characteristics: FBI confidential informant, FISA surveillance. Organization referenced in charging documents: Al Qaeda.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: Marine Corps University Treasonous Tides PDF Figure71 explicitly identifies Hassan Abu-Jihaad and cites military intelligence source. Needs extraction/rights inspection before ingestion; follow-up retained.

profiles.name: Linda Faith Greene
profiles.description: Linda Faith Greene, age 61, was indicted in 2009 for stalking and conspiracy to threaten UCLA scientists involved in animal research. Plea agreement: five years formal probation; she acknowledged being the press officer for the North American Animal Liberation Press Office.
profiles.finding: Daily Bruin case coverage corroborates identity; NABR guide mentions Linda Faith Green/Lindy but portrait not verified.

profiles.name: Robert Alford
profiles.description: Robert Alford was a U.S. servicemember who refused deployment during the Iraq/Afghanistan wars. Iraq War military refuser; pled guilty to desertion. Sentenced to short.
profiles.finding: Sparse profile prevents reliable identity match. Football player, Canadian politician, WWII serviceman and older obituary namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: William James Viehl
profiles.description: William James Viehl, age 23, pleaded guilty to AETA charges for the 2009 release of approximately 650 mink from a fur farm in South Jordan, Utah. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison plus $66,753 restitution.
profiles.finding: Denver ABC page explicitly labels William Viehl image sourced from Deseret News. Image https://i0.wp.com/www.deseretnews.com/photos/midres/902421.jpg returned404. Original newspaper image recovery lead retained.

profiles.name: Nathan Pope
profiles.description: Nathan Pope, age 26, was one of the AETA 4 - four young people indicted in 2009 under the Animal Enterprise Terrorism Act for protest activity targeting University of California researchers. The indictment was dismissed by the court for failing to specify the conduct.
profiles.finding: AETA dismissal and Denver ABC group-image lead corroborate defendant; group member position not verified. Pharmacist, minister and athlete namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Stevie Lynn Lowe
profiles.description: Stevie Lynn Lowe joined the Barley Barber Swamp protest in Florida. A jury acquitted her of trespassing but convicted her of resisting arrest without violence, resulting in jail time before release on appellate bond.
profiles.finding: PBCEC identifies Stevie and case but article image is Barley Barber sign. Commons inferred file URL404; Wikipedia file fetch failed. Flickr archive lead retained; no portrait added.

profiles.name: Leo Church
profiles.description: Leo Church was a U.S. Army soldier who went absent without leave to care for his children after learning that they were homeless. His lawyer described denied leave, inadequate childcare arrangements, and further absences. Church received an eight-month confinement sentence and a bad-conduct discharge. A December 2009 report confirmed his release from the Fort Lewis stockade. His refusal arose from family-care needs; the evidence does not establish a formal conscientious-objector claim.
profiles.finding: Courage to Resist corroborates Leo Church but article photo explicitly identifies Travis Bishop, so rejected for Church.
